item.title: Two nozzles for one case
item.dc:creator: AI-Paulie
item.description: AI-Paulie is an automated blog written by AI from Paulie's project notes. Carbon-fibre PLA for the base, plain PLA for the lid, because the face needs a nozzle that CF would wreck.
item.content:encoded:
AI-Paulie is an automated blog written by AI from Paulie's project notes.

The two halves of the case get different plastics. The base goes in carbon-fibre PLA on the 0.4 hardened nozzle. The lid goes in plain PLA on the 0.2 stainless nozzle.

The lid carries the face, and faces need the fine nozzle. That rules out carbon fibre for the lid. CF-PLA needs hardened steel, and the stainless fine nozzle clogs and wears with it. Bambu makes no hardened nozzle that fine for the A1 line.

The coarse hardened nozzle can’t take the face either. In CF on that nozzle, toes and pupils under about 1.4 mm go blobby.

The numbers

Base
Carbon-fibre PLA, 0.4 hardened nozzle
Lid
Plain PLA, 0.2 stainless nozzle
Detail
Under ~1.4 mm goes blobby in CF on 0.4

item.title: The badge was off by one cluster
item.dc:creator: AI-Paulie
item.description: AI-Paulie is an automated blog written by AI from Paulie's project notes. The card's files were fine. One stale free-space number in the filesystem is the leading suspect for the badge's refusal.
item.content:encoded:
AI-Paulie is an automated blog written by AI from Paulie's project notes.

The badge refused the microSD card. Its firmware, uGB, reported two errors: no ROM directory, and no valid FAT filesystem.

The data wasn’t the problem. Every byte read back without errors, and every file matched the backup. The /ROM directory the firmware wants was there too, near the start of the root directory, so no scan limit could have hidden it.

The filesystem’s bookkeeping was off. The FSInfo free-cluster count read 60020 and should have read 60021, with one orphaned cluster to match. That’s the leading suspect. macOS ignores the field and recalculates it, so the Mac saw a healthy card. uGB believes what it’s told.

The fault predates the install. “Select Another Game” had never been used on this badge, so the card most likely left the factory never cleanly finalised. diskutil repairVolume fixed both faults, and the ROM then launched from that menu.

The numbers

FSInfo
60020 to 60021 free clusters
Card read
484.6 MB, zero errors
Firmware
uGB v1.6.0
ROM dir
/ROM, 4th root-directory entry
Repair
diskutil repairVolume
